players.product: Atlas and Origin agentic target-to-antibody discovery platform

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Sean McClain: the ABS-201 pattern hair loss Phase II 13-week efficacy data will be announced in December of this year, with recruitment 'going extremely well'; the 26-week data are expected in early 2027. After the 26-week readout and safety data Absci plans to go to the FDA to begin registrational studies in 2027, while still collecting one-year post-dose durability data. He said roughly 1,500 patients will be needed for a safety database across all trials, and Absci internally estimates the per-patient trial cost at $60,000-$70,000.
quarterly_data.figure: 13-week data in December; 26-week data early 2027; roughly 1,500-patient safety database; $60,000-$70,000 per patient

quarterly_data.signal: CFO/CBO Zach Jonasson on the ABS-201 commercial case: a survey of 610 consumers with pattern hair loss, shown a target profile of about 30 hairs per square centimeter terminal hair growth (similar to high-dose oral minoxidil) with a couple of years' durability from three injections over six months, supports an estimated TAM north of $25 billion in the U.S. alone, with premium cash-pay pricing (no reimbursement planned, likely HSA-eligible). CEO: the plan is an at-home auto-injector distributed through dermatologists and telehealth partners in a direct-to-consumer model.
quarterly_data.figure: 610 consumers surveyed; north of $25 billion U.S. TAM at the target profile

quarterly_data.signal: Platform and cost model (management): the roughly $15 million per program covers all work from drug candidate through IND-enabling studies to Phase I readiness (CFO). CEO: the Atlas agentic co-scientist is surfacing 5-plus new targets per indication, and Absci is using China to test target hypotheses and for proof-of-concept and Phase II execution, running trials at a tenth of the cost. CFO: the goal is to start an endometriosis Phase II study this year, and current cash runs through the ABS-201 headline readout (26-week data and one-year follow-up) and at least the endometriosis interim readout.
quarterly_data.figure: $15 million per program to Phase I ready; 5-plus targets per indication; trials at a tenth of the cost

contracts.signal: CEO Sean McClain: Lilly's $40 million investment carries no rights to the asset in pattern hair loss or endometriosis and no option, right of first negotiation or governance rights ('tickets to the game'); a Lilly representative sits on the endometriosis advisory board.
